title: Supabase MCP server
summary: Supabase's MCP server, as identified in AVE-2026-0002. Both established capabilities depend on configuration the lock records as grants: what the credential can read, and whether the server is in read-only mode.

evidence.note: Run with the service_role key, the server bypasses all row-level security; the write-up has it reading a private integration_tokens table.
With writes allowed, the agent inserts private data into a table the attacker can read (support_messages). The write-up names the database write as the leg that communicates data to the attacker.

unknown.note: True in the write-up only because the database held customer-submitted support messages. Whether a given database holds rows outsiders can write is deployment data that a lock does not record.
Established only for the service_role credential. With a role subject to row-level security it depends on the policies, which the sources do not cover.

With readOnly true the source says read-only mode removes the write channel used in the attack. It does not say no other egress channel remains, so read-only is left unknown rather than recorded as false.
